sub_scenario.family: negotiating scope commitments when project evidence is incomplete
sub_scenario.one_line: heritage restoration officer: authorize diagnosis and interim protection

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the condition file and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The works diary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I authorized routine cleaning once the material and method were documented in the condition file.
Was a new intervention still disputed?
No, previous treatment records applied.
Someone new shadowed me in the restoration office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the conservation seasons into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

When the clocktower proposal showed surface staining in photographs but no mortar analysis, access survey, or water-entry confirmation, I told the conservation panel we could start a diagnostic survey and temporary weather protection while any permanent restoration waited on findings.
Why could restoration not be promised yet?
Different causes would require different work, and access may control what is possible.
I arranged a small stone repair last spring after the mason measured the affected edge.
Did that commit a full restoration?
No, we knew the loss, access method, and permitted scope.
I archived last cycle's notes on the works diary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The preservation fund can pay for a diagnostic survey and temporary weather protection.
Does it cover a full restoration package?
No, that would need a defined treatment and separate approval.
A vendor call about the condition file ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the restoration office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the conservation seasons.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the works diary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.

On a prior town-gate project, I promised full stone restoration before the anniversary from photographs alone; when the survey showed water ingress rather than mortar failure, the scaffold had to be reconfigured at extra cost.
What did the early promise assume?
That visible staining identified the governing cause and treatment.
I sketched next week's plan for the conservation seasons before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the condition file updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The town anniversary is four months away.
Does that justify choosing a treatment without analysis?
No, it makes temporary protection more useful while the cause is learned.
I compared two options for the works diary tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the restoration office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Can I commit to restoring the clocktower before the town anniversary?
